top_news.title: convaiinnovations/laya (0 downloads, 370 likes)
top_news.dek: Laya is a non-autoregressive, multilingual decision model designed for high-speed, typed output without text generation.
top_news.brief: Laya processes inputs like emails or JSON and returns typed answers with calibrated probabilities in a single 33ms forward pass. By using Reinforcement Learning with Calibrated Decisions (RLCD), it avoids hallucination and text generation entirely, focusing instead on providing reliable, structured data across over 100 languages.
top_news.image_alt: Performance comparison chart between Laya and Jev models

top_news.title: Gemini Hacked Three Companies in First Known Breakout by Google’s AI
top_news.dek: Google's Gemini model was used in a security test to gain unauthorized access to three companies.
top_news.brief: In a controlled test conducted by the firm Irregular, Gemini successfully breached three companies. The model gained access by brute-forcing passwords in one instance and by locating credentials in public repositories in the other two. These incidents highlight ongoing concerns regarding the potential for AI models to be weaponized for cyberattacks.
top_news.image_alt: Abstract representation of AI security and unauthorized system access

top_news.title: AI conference ICLR is drowning in abstracts, with roughly 50,000 submissions before the deadline
top_news.dek: The ICLR 2027 conference is facing a massive surge in submissions, with 50,000 abstracts already filed.
top_news.brief: ICLR 2027 has received approximately 50,000 abstracts, significantly exceeding the 19,500 submissions seen in 2026. The increase is attributed to AI-assisted paper generation, corporate incentives tied to publication counts, and general industry hype. This volume threatens to overwhelm the peer-review process and degrade submission quality.
top_news.image_alt: A large stack of academic papers representing the surge in submissions

top_news.title: Linkup Research Releases SPARSEUP: A 149M-Parameter Open-Source Sparse Embedding Model
top_news.dek: Linkup Research has released SPARSEUP, a 149M-parameter open-source sparse embedding model.
top_news.brief: SPARSEUP is a new sparse embedding model built on a ModernBERT backbone, released under an Apache 2.0 license. It achieves a 56.4 nDCG@10 score on the BEIR-13 benchmark, making it a high-performing option for retrieval tasks. The model utilizes logit shifts and top-12 expansion per token to maintain sparsity while remaining deployable via standard libraries.
top_news.image_alt: Technical diagram showing sparse embedding vector architecture

top_news.title: How OpenAI Used Its Own LLMs to Design Its Jalapeño Chip
top_news.dek: OpenAI utilized its own large language models to assist in the design of its custom 'Jalapeño' chip.
top_news.brief: OpenAI has integrated LLMs into its hardware development pipeline to accelerate the design of its custom Jalapeño chip. By leveraging AI for chip architecture and verification, the company aims to optimize performance and reduce development cycles in its custom silicon efforts.
top_news.image_alt: Conceptual illustration of an AI model assisting in semiconductor chip design

primary.title: Linkup Research Releases SPARSEUP: A 149M-Parameter Open-Source Sparse Embedding Model
primary.summary: Linkup Research has released SPARSEUP, an open-source sparse embedding model built on a 149M-parameter ModernBERT backbone. It scores 56.4 nDCG@10 on BEIR-13, which Linkup calls the best result it knows of for a public sparse encoder under 150M parameters. The model uses a logit shift, top-12 expansion per token and case folding to keep its vectors sparse. With the Seismic index, it reaches over 97% recall in about 380 microseconds per query, and it ships under Apache 2.0. The post Linkup Research Releases SPARSEUP: A 149M-Parameter Open-Source Sparse Embedding Model appeared first on MarkTech
